title: Flipping an active coordinate toggles the mod-2 inner product
statement: Let $x, y$ be $n$-bit Boolean inputs, and let $i$ be a coordinate at which $y_i = \mathtt{true}$. Write $\langle u, v\rangle = \bigoplus_{j} (u_j \wedge v_j)$ for the mod-2 inner product of two $n$-bit inputs, and let $x'$ denote the input agreeing with $x$ at every coordinate except $i$, where $x'_i = \lnot\, x_i$. Then \[ \langle x', y\rangle = \langle x, y\rangle \oplus \mathtt{true}, \] so negating the $i$-th coordinate of $x$ flips the value of the inner product.
hypotheses_covered: x, y are n-bit Boolean inputs
i is a coordinate index in Fin n
replaced:
If $y_i = \mathtt{true}$, then flipping coordinate $i$ of $x$ toggles the inner
product: $\mathrm{innerProduct}(n, \mathrm{flipAt}(i, x), y) =
\mathrm{innerProduct}(n, x, y) \oplus \mathtt{true}$.
